name: stkdefer
description: A SESSION SHELL SPAWNS A SESSION SHELL, AND BOTH COME BACK WHOLE.  Two session shells do not fit the arena side by side, and the only range the second can have is the first's -- which the first is standing on while it spawns.  So Task_AllocStack places the second OVER the first without clearing it: the image is built in the second's home image (the paint and the argv staging are pointed there) and the second starts out parked; when the scheduler first picks it, the first shell is in wait(), gets parked, and the second is brought in (Uimg_Ensure).  This is the case the B3 lane's spawn hand-off existed for, generalised to any range.  The inner shell echoes a value it can only have got from the outer shell's expansion, and the outer shell echoes its own variable again AFTER the inner has exited -- a restore that dropped a live byte of the outer's frames would not print OUTER=ok.  The klog must carry the deferred placement (stkdefer), a park (upark) and a restore (urest), and no refusal (upin): the mechanism is observed, not trusted.  The needles are built by expansion, so neither appears in anything typed.
command: tcsh -c 'set a=ok; tcsh -c "echo INNER=$a"; echo OUTER=$a'
